metadata.description: RTD plugin marketplace for Claude Code

plugins.name: oberskills
plugins.description: Prompt engineering, agent dispatch enforcement, skill creation and review, screenshot analysis, web search, and writing that doesn't sound like a robot wrote it. The skills I use every day, bundled up.

plugins.name: code-foundations
plugins.description: Software engineering habits pulled straight from the books that actually changed how I write code. Checklist-driven review, debugging, whiteboarding, and gates that keep quality honest.

plugins.name: design-for-ai
plugins.description: A four-stage design workflow, research, plan, mock, build, built on real doctrine instead of vibes. Seeded composition dealer, user-pinnable axes, dual-blind review, and gated artifacts so nothing ships half-baked.

plugins.name: react-native-foundations
plugins.description: Everything I reach for on React Native: docs search, iOS Simulator control, error diagnosis, runtime debugging, layout checks, accessibility audits, and coding guidance that's actually current.

plugins.name: svelte-foundations
plugins.description: The same kit for Svelte and SvelteKit: docs search, browser automation over CDP, error diagnosis, coding guidance, and accessibility audits.

plugins.name: claude-mux
plugins.description: An MCP server for tmux, so an agent can spawn workers, talk to them, share task lists, and run whole tmux sessions without me babysitting it.

plugins.name: grug-brain
plugins.description: Persistent memory for LLMs. FTS5 search, docs indexing, a dreaming pass, and brain sync across machines, all stored as plain markdown you can read and git-track yourself.

plugins.name: penman
plugins.description: Paste markdown, get it looking right everywhere: Slack, Teams, Discord, Notion, Word, Outlook, Gmail, Confluence, Jira, PowerPoint. Copies styled HTML straight to your clipboard, ready to paste.

plugins.name: what
plugins.description: Four skills for interrogating anything I'm working on: what-for draws out the real requirements, what-else spreads the options, what-if probes a plan for blind spots, what-breaks stress-tests the built thing. Each hands the work to a fresh Fable 5 agent and relays only the distilled result — the deliberation stays out of my context. Not just code: packs for writing, product, research, and life decisions load on demand.

plugins.name: systems-design
plugins.description: Frameworks I use for system design interviews and architecture review, built for distributed systems, not generic advice.

plugins.name: herderp
plugins.description: MCP tools for herdr and the Herdr desktop app (herdr-core), side by side: one set of agent, layout and watch tools across both, plus adopt to move a Claude Code session into the Herdr app. Then the fun part: necromancy. See which sessions died in a space and read them back.

plugins.name: sdd
plugins.description: Lets Claude hand a scoped job to another CLI or model and get a clean answer back. Eleven harnesses ship: codex, grok, kimi, qwen and mistral for second opinions, agy for review, implementation, images and video vision, the Gemini decision model for cheap batch yes/no, choice and score questions over text, images, video, audio or PDFs (plus an API-key video fallback when agy is out of quota), and a yt-dlp/whisper/ffmpeg/shazam pipeline that turns a video URL into a transcript, keyframes and a fused digest. Each one runs as a child process in your repo and reports back {status, summary, artifacts, raw}, so Claude stays the brain and keeps a clean diff. A spend ledger and budget show and cap what every job costs, usage puts Claude, Gemini and codex usage in one report, and helper agents (gemini-judge, video-digest, spend-watch, codex-builder, codex-reviewer) let loops do cheap work outside Claude quota.

plugins.name: siren
plugins.description: Mermaid diagrams that look like somebody made a decision, and that are right the first time. A semantic color palette so blue always means happy path and red always means failure, per-type quality checklists, and every silent-failure trap already mapped so you skip the render-fix-rerender loop. Ships a zero-dependency validator with 20 checks that catches what a render cannot, plus a no-build gallery site template with pan/zoom and export.

plugins.name: engram
plugins.description: Durable cross-session memory for Claude Code: hybrid search over episodic, semantic and graph memory on a self-hosted Engram server, with per-machine identities and opt-in sharing. Needs a running engramd, ENGRAM_ADDR/ENGRAM_TOKEN, and engram-mcp installed via go install.

plugins.name: domod
plugins.description: A todo list and notepad you and Claude share across sessions. Claude files the action items it leaves you, takes the ones you hand back, and closes them when the work is done. A pane, a line above the prompt and your status line show what's open; a small model sorts requests out of replies, decision items get go/no-go buttons, and items naming a PR close when it merges. Every feature has its own switch in /config.

plugins.name: proompt
plugins.description: Long prompts go through Haiku before Claude reads them and come out shorter: yours, the tasks Claude writes for subagents, SendMessage, and messages from other sessions. Paths, URLs, code, @-mentions and tags come through exactly, and any rewrite that loses one, answers instead of rewriting, or barely saves is thrown away for the original. /proompt last shows what you wrote beside what was sent.

plugins.name: destoopify
plugins.description: Fixes the spelling and grammar in what you type before Claude reads it, through Haiku, without rephrasing. Code, paths, URLs and slash commands stay exact; any failure or odd reply sends your original. A status line shows what it fixed; /destoopify turns it off or on.
